title: Runtimes
subtitle: Each user's own data plane: runs, flows, sessions and memory
note: A runtime is a user's own data plane: their runs, flows, sessions and memory. Each user gets one, named after them, unless an admin bound them to a shared one. Entities have their own too. Click a runtime to open its runs and cache below; the default runtime's cache also lists every machine-wide store.
teach: Select a runtime above — click a row — to load its runs and cache.
status_tip: Filter runs by their durable status
runs_search: Search runs — run id, workflow, session…
root_only_tip: Hide child runs — one row per top-level run
readonly_note: Read-only view — newest runs on this plane. Inspect/steer/cancel run through the default runtime's command lane and are not available here.
cancel_confirm: Cancel run {id}? Any in-flight work stops at the next tick.
steer_lead: Guidance folds into {id}'s next reasoning cycle (durable inbox — delivered at the loop boundary, never lost).
steer_placeholder: e.g. focus on the failing test first; prefer minimal diffs
artifacts_search: Search artifacts — name, kind, tags, date (YYYY-MM-DD)…
artifacts_note: Artifacts are indexed on the gateway store this console session reads (all planes).
caches_note: Disposable caches only — purging one just costs recomputation (re-download for model weights, re-encode for prompt KV). Durable stores are never listed here: deliverables live in the Artifacts tab, logs in the Logs tab.
purge_tip: Delete the CONTENTS of this cache; a dry-run accounting is shown first
forget_tip: Remove this stale registry row (disk untouched)
forget_all_tip: Remove every stale registry row in one go (disk untouched)
forget_confirm: This removes {l} from the data-home registry. Disk is never touched — the rows point at paths that no longer exist.
log_refresh_tip: Read the latest lines of this log again
